newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Kuehbacher says jobless rate threatens EMU.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Kuehbacher says jobless rate threatens EMU.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said on Friday that Germany's new record jobless rate would make it harder for Germany to join Europe's currency union on time at the end of the decade.

The high jobless rate, reaching 4.66 million people in January, will likely drive up social costs which will make it more difficult for the government to further consolidate its budget, Kuehbacher said at a banking congress here.

"This will endanger the government's plans of reaching a budget deficit of 2.9 percent of gross domestic product," Kuehbacher said. Maastricht criteria require the deficit to be below three percent of GDP.
Kuehbacher, also the president of the state central bank in Berlin and Brandenburg, said that government officials must take action, rather than only talking.

In order to join Europe's planned currency union at its scheduled launch date in 1999, nations must show that their budget deficits and government debts are under control, not exceeding strict targets.

The Bundesbank has on several occasions said that it cannot assist in reducing the nation's unemployment rate since the labour market suffers from structural problems that cannot be corrected by the central bank.
